messages:
maria: Customer report — long-lived SSE stream from Python SDK suddenly stops yielding (generator freezes) after ~45m. No exception in user code, connection still `200` on server side. Customer blocked, ticket #INC-7643. Repro + logs below.

jake: Thanks — can you confirm SDK version, python version, and a minimal repro? Also any proxy/load balancer in between?

maria: SDK: redwood-python 0.9.1 (customer originally on 0.8.8, tried upgrade). Python 3.10.8. No obvious LB, runs inside their k8s cluster behind nginx-ingress. Repro pattern: create stream, iterate generator, after many keepalives the generator yields nothing even though server continues to send heartbeats. No exception, iteration just blocks.

alex: Can you paste a tiny snippet showing how they consume the generator? Also include the last few debug logs from the client (set REDWOOD_DEBUG=stream).

maria: Minimal repro (trimmed):

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
gen = client.stream("chat.completions", model="gpt-lite", input="hello")
for chunk in gen:
    if chunk.get("type") == "message":
        print(chunk["text"], end="")
    # simple processing, no blocking io
```

Client logs (DEBUG=stream) around stall:
```
stream: recv event: data={...}
stream: processed event, appended to replay_buffer (len=40)
stream: keepalive batch received (n=4), replay_buffer len=44, total_bytes=16384
stream: retry triggered (5xx), replay_buffer retained for resume
stream: keepalive batch received (n=512), replay_buffer len=556, total_bytes=524288
stream: replay buffer exceeded soft limit (524288 > 524288), marking for compaction
stream: compaction skipped due to active retry_state
stream: generator yield loop waiting for next event
# no further yields though server continues sending keepalives
```

maria: Observations — when retries occur (5xx or network blips) the client preserves events in a replay buffer to resume. If a burst of keepalives arrives while retry_state is active the buffer grows and the generator stops delivering new items (freeze).

jake: That sounds like a replay-buffer-overrun + backpressure bug. In older SDKs we had a similar problem where compaction deferred while retry_state locked the buffer. Workaround: set `client._config.max_replay_buffer_bytes = 0` to disable buffering (not ideal), or increase retry backoff to avoid concurrent replay growth.

alex: Confirmed on local repro — two things: 1) keepalives are batched on the server into large frames which massively increases buffer size during retry; 2) when `retry_state` is non-idempotent we accidentally skip compaction. I'll open a runtime fix to drop oldest buffer entries when size > threshold. Putting a guard to avoid blocking the generator.

sre-oncall: Short-term mitigation for customers: 1) set REDWOOD_STREAM_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL to 30s (from 5s) on server side if possible; 2) apply SDK env `REDWOOD_SDK_MAX_REPLAY_BYTES=65536`; 3) bump client retry policy (exponential base 2 -> 8s). That reduces burst growth.

maria: Customer tried disabling buffering with the internal knob and the stream resumed reliably. They're asking for a patch and ETA.

alex: I filed issue #453 (runtime: replay-buffer compaction race) and a PR draft that implements an eviction policy (drop oldest frames while keeping resume markers). PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt/pull/789 (draft). I expect to have a tested patch by EOD tomorrow and a canary release after QA.

maria: Great — can you include clear repro steps and the minimal script above so I can validate with the customer? Also need an escalation note for their SOC — they want to know if any data loss is possible.

alex: Repro steps in the PR description. Data loss: short answer — in current behavior some keepalive-only frames may be dropped by eviction (we will preserve user-visible messages). We'll document exactly which event types may be evicted and add audit logs.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-7643 linked to issue #453. Assigned: alex, priority: P1.

maria: Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll keep the customer updated and request access for a remote session to run the patched canary when ready.
